method: Triangulation of live first-party employer descriptions, official platform and open-source documentation, standards guidance, and primary research. Job descriptions establish title usage and accountability; documentation and papers establish durable technical work, limitations, and boundaries. No source alone defines the role.

sources.title: LLM Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact title and assigns RAG, intelligent search, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, prompt design, guardrails, and output evaluation.
sources.limitations: Consulting role centered on one enterprise search pattern; does not represent model training at frontier scale.

sources.title: LLM Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the exact title for implementing LLM research in end-user applications, designing evaluation frameworks, integrating models and parameters, and iterating from client feedback.
sources.limitations: Hiring-agent product combines LLM and agent responsibilities; organization-specific division of labor.

sources.title: Senior AI and LLM Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Uses the title for architecture, implementation, integration, fine-tuning, and domain-specific LLM systems in semiconductor design automation.
sources.limitations: Senior, domain-specific role; the combined AI/LLM label shows title variation.

sources.title: LLM Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Defines a tight fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment loop with ownership of data pipelines and adaptation architecture.
sources.limitations: Early-stage AI-native company; broad ownership may exceed a specialized role in a larger organization.

sources.title: Software Engineer II - GenAI / LLM Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Assigns production LLM components, RAG, embeddings/vector stores/reranking, model upgrades, fallback/latency incidents, and agent integrations to a software-engineering role.
sources.limitations: One Azure-oriented supply-chain environment; transient tool names are not durable competencies.

sources.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Proactive - Large Language Models & Generative AI Inference
sources.role: Machine Learning Engineer specializing in LLM systems
sources.evidence_summary: Shows LLM-specialist work under an MLE title: applying research, developing a high-performance model-serving stack, supporting product clients, optimizing inference, and setting technical direction.
sources.limitations: Demonstrates alias/overlap rather than exact-title usage and is strongly centered on inference-platform collaboration.

sources.title: Machine Learning Engineer II, AGI Customization
sources.role: ML Engineer specializing in LLM post-training
sources.evidence_summary: Assigns LLM customization capabilities—fine-tuning, distillation, model evaluation, and prompt optimization—and development of novel training techniques to an MLE collaborating with applied scientists.
sources.limitations: Frontier-scale customization is one end of the role spectrum and sits explicitly inside Machine Learning Engineering at this employer.

sources.title: LLM Ops Engineer
sources.evidence_summary: Shows an operations-heavy variant spanning fine-tuning data, APIs, model serving, scaling, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
sources.limitations: Explicitly an LLM Ops team; generalized platform ownership is adjacent rather than universal LLM Engineer core.

sources.title: Model optimization
sources.evidence_summary: Documents a recurring model-behavior optimization loop: establish evals, improve prompts/context, fine-tune when warranted, and repeat because outputs and model snapshots vary.
sources.limitations: Provider-specific product documentation; the decision loop is durable but APIs and supported methods change.

sources.title: Working with evals
sources.evidence_summary: Treats evaluation as a versioned engineering workflow over representative data, graders, runs, and model/application changes.
sources.limitations: Provider-specific implementation; does not independently validate a job title.

sources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations
sources.evidence_summary: Requires task-specific success criteria, empirical tests, multidimensional evaluation, representative edge cases, and iteration rather than anecdotal prompt inspection.
sources.limitations: Provider documentation; recommendations need context-specific validation.

sources.title: Introduction to tuning
sources.evidence_summary: Frames tuning as a decision after prompting/evaluation, distinguishes parameter-efficient and full tuning, and emphasizes high-quality representative labeled data.
sources.limitations: Managed-service documentation and currently supported model lists are volatile.

sources.title: Develop a generative AI application
sources.evidence_summary: Connects model selection/customization, datasets, automatic and human evaluation, production development, and responsible testing while stating limits of model-based evaluation.
sources.limitations: Cloud-specific workflow; some service behavior is not portable.

sources.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods
sources.evidence_summary: Documents prompt, layer, and adapter adaptation choices, their resource/expressivity tradeoffs, and the need to measure retention and runtime implications.
sources.limitations: Implementation documentation follows a fast-moving open-source library and is not a role definition.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.author_or_org: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.evidence_summary: Defines generative-AI-specific risks and lifecycle actions across governance, mapping, measurement, and management; supports the engineer's obligation to produce risk evidence without granting formal risk authority.
sources.limitations: Voluntary cross-sector guidance, not a profession standard or legal compliance determination.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.evidence_summary: Primary source for the transformer architecture, supporting enough internal understanding to reason about tokens, attention, context, computation, and limits.
sources.limitations: Predates current LLM scale and does not prescribe production engineering practice.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.evidence_summary: Primary source for combining parametric and non-parametric memory, motivating retrieval as a distinct behavior and evidence surface rather than a prompt trick.
sources.limitations: Original experimental formulation differs from many modern production RAG systems.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.evidence_summary: Primary source for low-rank adaptation and its training/deployment motivation; supports adaptation tradeoff analysis rather than universal LoRA use.
sources.limitations: Results are model/task-specific and later techniques may outperform it.

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
sources.evidence_summary: Primary evidence that post-training data, reward modeling, human preferences, and evaluation materially shape language-model behavior.
sources.limitations: One research program and model family; not a universal recipe or safety guarantee.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.evidence_summary: Primary source for a preference-optimization alternative that exposes method, data, and objective choices in post-training.
sources.limitations: Research assumptions and benchmark results require reproduction for a target setting.

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
sources.evidence_summary: Primary source for memory-efficient adaptation of quantized models and the interaction among precision, training resources, and measured quality.
sources.limitations: Hardware, model, optimizer, and dataset assumptions constrain generalization.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
sources.evidence_summary: Primary evidence that memory movement and kernel design materially affect attention performance, supporting inference literacy without making kernel implementation universal role core.
sources.limitations: Hardware/software support and later implementations evolve; deep kernel work belongs to performance/infrastructure specialists.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
sources.evidence_summary: Provides a taxonomy-driven evaluation approach spanning scenarios and metrics, demonstrating why one benchmark or aggregate score cannot establish deployment fitness.
sources.limitations: Benchmark coverage and models age; task-specific evidence remains necessary.

claims.statement: LLM Engineer is a current standalone title used by independent employers across consulting, enterprise software, productivity, semiconductors, and AI-native products.
claims.limitations: The title is not standardized; employers also use AI/LLM Engineer, GenAI Engineer, ML Engineer, NLP Engineer, or Software Engineer for similar work.

claims.statement: Employer evidence converges on a language-model lifecycle spanning context/retrieval, data, adaptation, evaluation, software integration, deployment, and iterative improvement.
claims.limitations: No employer assigns every lifecycle stage to one individual; team topology changes the depth.

claims.statement: The role's durable unit of accountability is measured language-model behavior under defined task, data, context, adaptation, and runtime constraints—not the existence of a prompt or model endpoint.
claims.limitations: This is a synthesis across sources rather than language used verbatim by one employer.

claims.statement: Evaluation is a core development loop for LLM engineering because model behavior is probabilistic, multidimensional, task-dependent, and change-sensitive.
claims.limitations: Evaluation methods differ by consequence, task, modality, model access, and available human expertise.

claims.statement: Professional depth includes deciding among prompting, context/retrieval, supervised or preference tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation, distillation/quantization, or no adaptation, then validating the decision.
claims.limitations: Not every practitioner has access to model weights or large-scale training; provider-managed and open-weight paths require different depth.

claims.statement: LLM systems require explicit inference and operational tradeoffs among quality, context length, latency, throughput, memory, cost, capacity, and failure behavior.
claims.limitations: Deep serving-platform and kernel ownership belongs to adjacent infrastructure/performance roles.

claims.statement: Security, privacy, misuse, provenance, and responsible behavior must be designed and tested across data, context, model, output, and integration boundaries.
claims.limitations: Engineering controls and evidence do not grant legal, safety, privacy, security, compliance, or risk-acceptance authority.

claims.statement: An adaptation experiment is credible only when its data lineage, baselines, evaluation splits, retention/regression behavior, resource cost, and reproducibility limits are visible.
claims.limitations: Exact experimental controls depend on access, task consequence, and optimization method.

claims.statement: Agentic behavior is a frequent application surface for LLM engineers but planning, tool authorization, durable state, multi-agent coordination, and action recovery define the separate Agentic AI Engineer specialization.
claims.limitations: Employers frequently combine the roles; boundary is based on primary accountability, not tool use.

claims.statement: Safety, security, governance, and evaluation specialists retain independent authority and deeper cross-system methods even when LLM engineers implement controls and produce evidence.
claims.limitations: Organization-specific authority must be documented; NIST guidance does not define job reporting lines.

claims.statement: Machine Learning Engineer is broader across model families and the ML lifecycle; LLM Engineer is deeper in language-model behavior, token/context interfaces, post-training, and generative evaluation.
claims.limitations: Many organizations place LLM specialization inside the MLE title family.

claims.statement: Applied AI Engineer owns a broader product/system behavior loop across AI mechanisms; LLM Engineer owns deeper language-model-specific behavior and adaptation decisions.
claims.limitations: Small teams may combine both accountabilities.

claims.statement: AI Research Engineer creates or validates generally novel capabilities; LLM Engineer reproduces, adapts, evaluates, and operationalizes methods for a defined language-model system.
claims.limitations: Frontier teams intentionally blur research and engineering.

claims.statement: MLOps, ML platform, inference, and AI performance engineers own generalized pipelines, serving platforms, fleet economics, schedulers, and kernels; LLM engineers consume or co-design these to meet one model-system behavior contract.
claims.limitations: In smaller teams, one engineer may own both application/model behavior and generalized infrastructure.

claims.statement: Role depth spans provider-managed model integration through open-weight post-training and serving, so competence must be expressed as decisions and evidence rather than mandatory access to frontier training compute.
claims.limitations: A single assessment must state the expected access posture for each scenario.

claims.statement: Models, APIs, frameworks, tuning libraries, evaluation services, and serving runtimes change quickly; durable teaching must organize them around contracts, experiments, failure modes, and change control.
claims.limitations: Current examples still require edition-level verification.

claims.statement: Advanced LLM engineers lead behavior and adaptation strategy, evaluation standards, model-change decisions, and cross-functional evidence while preserving specialist and formal authority boundaries.
claims.limitations: Leadership scope varies more than implementation scope and is skewed by senior postings.

claims.statement: The role requires enough transformer, tokenization, attention, adaptation, preference, quantization, and inference literacy to predict consequences and diagnose evidence, without requiring novel foundation-model research or kernel invention.
claims.limitations: Required mathematical and systems depth changes by role posture.
